title: Implement sequential keyboard shortcuts with Alt
author: eylenburg
body:
If you work in an industry like finance or accounting, you'll see people who have memorised hundreds of keyboard shortcuts for Excel. You  can use every function in Excel without ever using the mouse. 

In Excel, when you press "Alt", there are tooltips on the ribbon which you can sequentially press. e.g. you Alt -> H [Home] -> A [Align] -> R [Right] allows you to apply "Align Right" formatting.  Alt -> H -> V -> S opens the "Paste Special" menu where you can then use more shortcuts without ever using the mouse, e.g. Alt + E for transpose paste. You can use this for anything on the ribbon, no matter how deep down in some submenu it is.

There are also other shortcuts started with Alt and sequential key presses. I think a lot of them come from pre-ribbon Excel. For example, Alt -> E -> S -> T/V/F/C pastest only Formatting/Values/Formulas/Comments, respectively. Or Alt -> O -> C -> A is a legacy shortcut for auto-fit column width (the shortcut based on ribbon tooltips would be Alt -> H -> O -> I). 

The end goal of should be not only to implement sequential shortcuts starting with Alt, but generally making Gridcraft usable completely without mouse while using the exact same keyboard shortcuts as Excel.

title: Feature request: Spanish-localized formula function names and separators
author: funkholio
body:
## Summary

Please add support for Spanish-localized formula syntax in GridCraft.

Currently, formulas appear to require English function names and comma-separated arguments. This makes GridCraft harder to use for Spanish-speaking users and reduces compatibility with workbooks created in localized versions of Microsoft Excel or LibreOffice Calc.

## Requested functionality

Allow GridCraft to recognize Spanish aliases for Excel-compatible function names, while preserving English function names as the canonical/internal syntax.

Examples:

| Spanish formula | English equivalent |
|---|---|
| `=SUMA(A1:A10)` | `=SUM(A1:A10)` |
| `=PROMEDIO(A1:A10)` | `=AVERAGE(A1:A10)` |
| `=SI(A1>0;"Sí";"No")` | `=IF(A1>0,"Sí","No")` |
| `=SUMAR.SI(A1:A10;">0")` | `=SUMIF(A1:A10,">0")` |
| `=CONTAR.SI(A1:A10;">0")` | `=COUNTIF(A1:A10,">0")` |
| `=BUSCARV(A2;D:E;2;FALSO)` | `=VLOOKUP(A2,D:E,2,FALSE)` |
| `=HOY()` | `=TODAY()` |
| `=VERDADERO` / `=FALSO` | `=TRUE` / `=FALSE` |

## Separator support

For Spanish locales, please also consider accepting semicolons (`;`) as function argument separators, in addition to commas (`,`).

For example:

```excel
=SI(A1>100;"Alto";"Bajo")
```

could be interpreted equivalently to:

```excel
=IF(A1>100,"Alto","Bajo")
```

## Why this matters

Spanish is widely used across Latin America and Spain. Supporting localized function aliases would:

- Improve usability for Spanish-speaking users.
- Help users migrate existing Excel and LibreOffice spreadsheets.
- Improve formula compatibility with localized spreadsheet workflows.
- Allow GridCraft to remain internally English-based while providing locale-aware parsing and display.

A first implementation could focus on a small set of common functions (`SUMA`, `SI`, `PROMEDIO`, `CONTAR`, `SUMAR.SI`, `BUSCARV`) and expand over time.

Thank you for considering it.

title: Rotated text with Wrap Text on is drawn horizontally (grid and print)
author: LloydNicholson
body:
Cells with **both** a text rotation (e.g. 90°, `textRotation="90"`) **and** Wrap Text on are drawn horizontally: the rotation is ignored and the text is word-wrapped into the column width instead. This is common in mark sheets and schedules, where narrow columns have tall, upright headers.

**Repro** (no real data needed):
```sh
gridcraft-cli run --cmd 'cell.set={"cell":"A1","input":"Term 1 : Drama : Continuous Assessment"}' \
  --cmd 'home.orientation={"range":"A1","angle":"up"}' \
  --cmd 'home.wrapText={"range":"A1","on":true}' \
  --cmd 'home.columnWidth={"cols":"A:A","chars":4}' \
  --cmd 'home.rowHeight={"rows":"1:1","height":267}' --out rotated.xlsx
gridcraft rotated.xlsx
```
The same happens opening an `.xlsx` saved elsewhere with `<alignment textRotation="90" wrapText="1"/>` on narrow columns.

**Expected:** the text reads bottom-to-top inside the tall cell (wrapping, if needed, along the rotated direction). Rotation without wrap already works.

**Actual:** horizontal text broken into 3–4 characters per line ("Ter / m 1 / Dra / ma…").

**Cause:** in `crates/ui-egui/src/grid.rs`, the wrap branch draws the galley and `continue`s before the rotated-text path is reached. `crates/engine/src/cmd/print.rs` has the same gap (`if rot != 0 && rot != 255 && !wrap`), so printing/PDF is affected too.

**Environment:** Fedora 44 x86_64, gridcraft `main` @ 51b531b (0.3.0).

I'm preparing a PR for this.

title: General numbers in small fonts show #### in narrow columns though they fit
author: LloydNicholson
body:
In narrow columns, General-format numbers in a font smaller than 11pt show `####` even though they fit. Common in mark sheets: 9pt marks such as `100` in columns with a stored width of 4 (28px).

**Repro** (no real data needed):
```sh
gridcraft-cli run --cmd 'cell.set={"cell":"A1","input":"100"}' \
  --cmd 'home.fontSize={"range":"A1","size":9}' \
  --cmd 'home.columnWidth={"cols":"A:A","width":28}' --out narrow.xlsx
gridcraft narrow.xlsx
```
**Expected:** `100` (it is ~16px wide at 9pt × the 0.8 display scale, in a 22.4px column). Printing already shows `100`.
**Actual:** `##`.

**Cause:** `grid.rs` measures the digit width once, for an 11pt cell font (`char_w`), and `display_text` decides how many General digits fit from that, whatever the cell's own font size. At 9pt the real digit is ~20% narrower, so `100` is judged 2 digits wide at most. (`print.rs` already measures with the cell's own font and size.)

**Environment:** Fedora 44 x86_64, gridcraft `main` @ 51b531b (0.3.0).

I'm preparing a PR for this.

title: `=0.1+0.2=0.3` returns FALSE: comparisons, MATCH and COUNTIF don't use Excel's 15-significant-digit equality
author: wzsxb233
body:
**Summary**

Excel and LibreOffice treat two numbers as equal when they agree to 15 significant digits, so floating-point noise doesn't break comparisons. GridCraft compares raw f64 values. As a result, common spreadsheet logic gives different answers from Excel. Examples are `IF(A1+A2=A3, …)`, exact `MATCH`, and `COUNTIF(range, 0.3)`. These formulas look right because the cells display `0.3`.

**Environment**
- GridCraft `main` @ 51b531b (v0.3.0), `gridcraft-cli` release build
- Linux x86_64 (Debian 13), Rust 1.99
- Reference: LibreOffice 25.2.3 headless recalculation of the same .xlsx

**Steps to reproduce**
```sh
gridcraft-cli eval '=0.1+0.2=0.3'                              # FALSE
gridcraft-cli eval '=1.1*3=3.3'                                # FALSE
gridcraft-cli eval '=IF(0.7+0.1=0.8,"eq","ne")'                # ne
gridcraft-cli eval '=MATCH(0.3,{0.1,0.30000000000000004},0)'   # #N/A
gridcraft-cli eval '=COUNTIF({0.30000000000000004},0.3)'       # 0
```
Workbook version: put `=0.1+0.2` in B1, then use `=COUNTIF(B1:B1,0.3)` and `=MATCH(0.3,B1:B1,0)`. `gridcraft-cli cat` shows B1 as `0.3`, but the formulas return `0` and `#N/A`.

**Expected** (Excel and LibreOffice)
`TRUE`, `TRUE`, `eq`, `2` and `1`. LibreOffice gives these results for the same workbook (`soffice --convert-to csv`).

**Actual**
`FALSE`, `FALSE`, `ne`, `#N/A` and `0`.

**Notes**
Excel compares values after rounding them to 15 significant digits. LibreOffice does the same with `rtl::math::approxEqual`. Applying this to `=`, `<>`, `<`, `>`, `<=` and `>=`, and to the exact-match paths of MATCH, XLOOKUP, VLOOKUP, COUNTIF and SUMIF, would match both apps. Related: ROUND to 15 or more digits also leaves the noise in place (separate issue).

title: ROUND(x, n) returns x unchanged when n reaches 15 significant digits: `ROUND(0.1+0.2,15)` = 0.30000000000000004
author: wzsxb233
body:
**Summary**

`round_half_away` (`crates/functions/src/util.rs`) builds a 15-significant-digit decimal string. When the requested digits reach the end of that string (`keep >= d.len()`), it returns the original `x`, not the 15-digit value. So `ROUND(x,15)` and similar calls, which people use to remove floating-point noise, leave the noise in place. In Excel, `ROUND(0.1+0.2,15)=0.3` is TRUE.

**Environment**
- GridCraft `main` @ 51b531b (v0.3.0), `gridcraft-cli` release build; Linux x86_64

**Steps to reproduce**
```sh
gridcraft-cli eval '=ROUND(0.1+0.2,15)'               # 0.30000000000000004
gridcraft-cli eval '=ROUND(0.1+0.2,15)-0.3'           # 5.551115123125783e-17
gridcraft-cli eval '=ROUND(0.1+0.2,15)=0.3'           # FALSE
gridcraft-cli eval '=ROUND(1.0000000000000002,15)=1'  # FALSE
gridcraft-cli eval '=ROUND(0.1+0.2,14)=0.3'           # TRUE (works below 15 digits)
```

**Expected**
`ROUND(0.1+0.2,15)` should return 0.3, and the comparisons should be TRUE, as in Excel and LibreOffice (LibreOffice checked headless).

**Actual**
The unrounded value is returned whenever `e + 1 + digits >= 15`.

**Suggested fix**
In the `keep >= d.len()` branch, return the value parsed back from the 15-significant-digit string, for example `format!("{:.14e}", x).parse()`, not `x`. The same probably applies to ROUNDUP/ROUNDDOWN if they share this helper.

title: XLSX writer omits `_xlpm.` prefix on LET/LAMBDA parameter names, so Excel refuses to open the file
author: nihilist-narwhal
body:
## Summary

Workbooks containing `LET` or `LAMBDA` are written with bare parameter names, e.g.

```xml
<f>_xlfn.LET(x,Data!A3*2,y,x+1,x*y)</f>
<f>_xlfn.LAMBDA(a,b,a^2+b)(3,4)</f>
```

In the file format Excel expects the parameter names to carry the `_xlpm.` prefix:

```xml
<f>_xlfn.LET(_xlpm.x,Data!A3*2,_xlpm.y,_xlpm.x+1,_xlpm.x*_xlpm.y)</f>
<f>_xlfn.LAMBDA(_xlpm.a,_xlpm.b,_xlpm.a^2+_xlpm.b)(3,4)</f>
```

Without it, Excel refuses to open the whole workbook, so a single `LET` anywhere makes a GridCraft-saved file unopenable in Excel.

## Repro

1. In GridCraft, set any cell to `=LET(x,2,x*3)` (or `=LAMBDA(a,a+1)(1)`).
2. Save as `.xlsx`.
3. Open in Excel → the file does not open.

I bisected a 108-formula test workbook one formula per file: only the `LET` and `LAMBDA` files are rejected. title: Non-spilling array formulas are saved without the dynamic-array flag (`cm`), so Excel applies implicit intersection: `SUM(A1:A20*B1:B20)` becomes `#VALUE!`
author: nihilist-narwhal
body:
## Summary

The XLSX writer marks a formula as dynamic-array (`cm="1"` + `xl/metadata.xml` `XLDAPR`) only when the formula **spills**. A formula that returns a single value but relies on array evaluation of ranges is written without the marker, so Excel loads it as a pre-dynamic-array formula and applies implicit intersection, which changes its result.

## Repro

`Data!A1:A20` and `Data!B1:B20` hold numbers; on another sheet, in row 107:

```
=SUM(Data!A1:A20*Data!B1:B20)
```

- GridCraft: `165321.5` (array evaluation, which is what Excel 365 gives when the formula is typed in)
- Same file opened and fully recalculated in Excel: `#VALUE!`, i.e. Excel treats it as a legacy formula, as if written `=SUM(@Data!A1:A20*@Data!B1:B20)`

Written XML:

```xml
<c r="B107"><f>SUM(Data!A1:A20*Data!B1:B20)</f>...
```

So the same workbook gives different numbers in GridCraft and in Excel after a round trip. Formulas whose array-ness comes from a "new" function (`SUM(FILTER(...))`, `ROWS(UNIQUE(...))`) or from `SUMPRODUCT` / `INDEX(...,0)` are fine; the problem is ordinary operators or functions applied to ranges where a scalar is expected.

## Where

`crates/xlsx/src/sheet_write.rs`, `write_cell`: `cm="1"` is written only when `dynamic.is_some()` (a spill range exists). As far as I can tell Excel 365 marks any formula whose legacy evaluation would differ (one that would need an `@` in an older Excel), not only spilling ones.

## The reading side

The converse also seems to hold: a formula in an Excel-authored file **without** `cm` is a legacy formula, and Excel evaluates it with implicit intersection. GridCraft evaluates it with array semantics, so on such files GridCraft will show `165321.5` where Excel shows `#VALUE!` (or a different scalar, when the range intersects the formula's row/column). Possibly the reader should keep a "legacy" flag (or insert `@`) for formulas without `cm`.

GridCraft `51b531b` (main), Excel for Mac 16.113.2, macOS 26.3. Found while dif…

title: Recalculation is quadratic in range formulas: large sheets take minutes to open or edit
author: LloydNicholson
body:
Recalculation time grows quadratically with the number of range formulas, so large sheets take minutes to open or edit. The values are correct; only the time is affected.

**Repro:** a sheet with `=SUM(E{r}:J{r})` on every row (no real data needed; any numbers in E:J).

| Rows | Headless open + recalc |
|---|---|
| 12.5k | 0.4 s |
| 25k | 1.5 s |
| 50k | 8.6 s |

A 50k-row × 20-column workbook takes about 65 s to open in the app. Editing a cell that 100k formulas depend on freezes the UI for about 30 s. Filling 50k formulas down takes over a minute.

**Expected:** roughly linear time; Excel opens these in about a second.

**Cause** (profiled):
- `Evaluator::trim` calls `Sheet::used_range` on every range read, and that walks every stored row, so a full recalc costs rows × range formulas.
- `Graph::dependents` scans each column's whole list of range precedents, and removing a formula runs a `retain` over it (`crates/calc/src/recalc.rs`), which makes fill, paste and sort quadratic.

**Environment:** macOS 26.6.2 arm64, gridcraft `main` @ 51b531b (0.3.0).

Fix in #66.

title: SUMIF/AVERAGEIF with a smaller sum_range give wrong totals
author: LloydNicholson
body:
`SUMIF` / `AVERAGEIF` with a sum range smaller than the criteria range give wrong totals. Excel uses a range that starts at sum_range's top-left cell and has the criteria range's size; GridCraft only uses the cells actually given.

**Repro:** A1:B3 = `a, 1` / `b, 2` / `a, 3`.

| Formula | Expected (Excel) | Actual |
|---|---|---|
| `=SUMIF(A1:A3,"a",B1)` | 4 | 1 |
| `=AVERAGEIF(A1:A3,"a",B1)` | 2 | 1 |
| `=SUMIF(A1:A3,"a",B1:B2)` | 4 | 1 |

**Cause:** `if_numbers` (`crates/functions/src/math.rs`) gets the sum range's values, not its reference, so it can't resize. Its comment says it does.

**Environment:** macOS 26.6.2 arm64, gridcraft `main` @ 51b531b (0.3.0).

Fix in #67.

title: DATE(1900,2,29) returns 61 instead of 60
author: LloydNicholson
body:
In the 1900 date system, Excel (following Lotus 1-2-3) keeps 29 February 1900 as serial 60, and `DAY(60)` already returns 29. But turning that date back into a serial gives a different number:

| Formula | Expected (Excel) | Actual |
|---|---|---|
| `=DATE(1900,2,29)` | 60 | 61 |
| `=DATEVALUE("2/29/1900")` | 60 | 61 |
| `=DATE(1900,3,0)` | 60 | 59 |
| `=EOMONTH(60,0)` | 60 | 59 (before its own input) |

Typing `2/29/1900` into a cell also stores 61.

**Cause:** `serial_from_ymd` (`crates/core/src/date.rs`) works out the real calendar date (1 March) and then shifts serials up to 60, so it can never produce 60.

Only dates in January–February 1900 are affected.

**Environment:** macOS 26.6.2 arm64, gridcraft `main` @ 51b531b (0.3.0).

Fix in #68.

title: macOS: workbook opened from Finder shows a format error and freezes the app
author: DDKatch
body:
## What happens

GridCraft is the default app for `.xlsx`. The user double-clicks a workbook in Finder.

- macOS shows an alert: *"GridCraft cannot open files in the 'Excel Workbook' format."*
- The alert is modal. The app never creates its first window, so it looks frozen.
- Dock-icon reopen (clicking the Dock icon while the app runs with no windows) does nothing.

Both reproduce with `open -a GridCraft.app workbook.xlsx`.

## Cause

Two layers.

1. **winit 0.30 handles no Apple Events.** The `odoc` event ("open documents") reaches the Apple Event Manager and finds no handler, so macOS runs its built-in document handler. That path ends in `NSDocumentController`, which cannot open a workbook and shows the alert.
2. **The launch case is worse.** On current macOS, documents passed at launch never reach `NSAppleEventManager` at all. LaunchServices hands them to AppKit, AppKit asks the app delegate to answer `application:openURLs:` (and the `openFiles:` / `openFile:` variants), and with no answer falls back to `NSDocumentController` — the same modal alert, this time before the first frame exists.

Because of layer 2, registering an `NSAppleEventManager` handler early cannot fix Finder opens: the event never arrives there. (An early registration alone also does not survive AppKit installing its own default handlers at `finishLaunching`.)

## Fix

New crate `gridcraft-macos-events` (PR to follow):

- Adds `application:openURLs:`, `application:openFiles:`, `application:openFile:` and `applicationShouldHandleReopen:` to `NSObject`, process-local. winit's delegate inherits them, so launch-time and running-instance opens land in the crate's queue.
- Registers `NSAppleEventManager` handlers for `odoc` / `rapp` as a second path (AppleScript, and `open` targeting a running instance).
- The app polls the queue each frame and opens the paths; Dock reopen opens the last workbook when no document is open.

The crate is the repository's single `unsafe` module: the Apple Event and del…

author: arhammusheer
body:
I'd like to take on calc performance and scaling, in five reviewable PRs. I'm posting the plan first so it doesn't collide with other work in `crates/calc`. If you're already changing the recalc scheduler or range evaluation, please say so here and we can split the work.

## Where it stands (upstream `main` at 90b3c41, Apple M2 Pro, release build)

I measured these with an extended `crates/engine/examples/perf.rs`, which comes with the first PR. Every scenario runs through `Session::execute` and checks its answer.

| Scenario | Time |
|---|---|
| 10k exact VLOOKUPs over a 10k-row table | 2.6 s |
| 10k XLOOKUPs / 10k MATCHes | 3.2 s / 2.1 s |
| Edit one table cell with 30k dependent lookups | 5.8 s |
| 1,000 × `SUM(A:A)` over 50k rows, then one edit | 0.65 s / 0.65 s |
| 20k-cell chain where each cell reads the one below it | wrong result: `#CIRC!` |

Lookups scale as O(n²): every range read copies the range (`range_values` returns a fresh `Vec<Value>`), and every exact match then scans it. The reverse chain fails because `PassHost::compute` treats recursion depth above 2,000 as a cycle (`recalc.rs`, `self.depth > 2000`). The same recursion overflows the stack and aborts the process with heavier formulas at around 1,000 cells, and `catch_unwind` can't catch a stack overflow.

## Plan

1. **Topological scheduler.** Order the dirty set with Kahn's algorithm over the existing graph, and evaluate it iteratively. Only real cycles become circular. On-demand evaluation stays for dynamic references (INDIRECT, OFFSET). Reverse chains become correct, the depth limit and the stack overflow go away, and we get dependency levels for step 3.
2. **Shared ranges and a lookup index.** Materialise each distinct range once per pass and share it. Build an exact-match hash index or sorted index once per lookup range and reuse it, as Excel 365 does for VLOOKUP/MATCH. Target: 100k lookups in about 1 s.

title: Feature request: AutoSave with pluggable storage (local folder, Google Drive, OneDrive, S3/R2 via rclone), version history, and a path to self-hosted co-editing
author: fernandodilland
body:
## TL;DR

In Excel, AutoSave, Version History and co-authoring only work when the file lives on OneDrive/SharePoint. ROADMAP.md says features that need Microsoft cloud services (e.g. co-authoring through OneDrive) will be replaced by open equivalents or left out. This issue proposes that open equivalent: a single, central **"Save target"** setting so a workbook can autosave to storage the user owns (local/NAS folder, Google Drive, OneDrive, S3-compatible such as Cloudflare R2, or anything rclone supports), with automatic version history, a lease/lock file to prevent overwrites, and an optional later phase for real-time co-editing (P2P or relay).

Principles: local-first, opt-in, no GridCraft-run servers, no telemetry, never lose data.

title: [Bug] Formatted tables do not automatically expand when entering adjacent data
author: AlissonFA
body:
### Problem Description
    
When working with formatted tables (`ListObject`), entering data into cells directly adjacent to the table (in the row immediately below or the column immediately to the right) does not expand the table boundaries.
    
In other programs, tables are designed to automatically grow as data is entered, maintaining data integrity by extending calculated columns, cell formatting, and validation rules. In GridCraft, entries in adjacent cells remain plain disconnected cells outside the table, requiring manual resizing and manual formula copying.
    
### Steps to Reproduce
    
1. Create a table with headers and data (e.g., in range `A1:C3`), where column `C` contains a formula (e.g., `=A2*B2`).
2. Type a value into cell `A4` (the row immediately below the table).
3. Observe the table boundaries and the cells in row 4.
4. Alternatively, type a value into cell `D2` (the column immediately to the right of the table).
    
### Expected Behavior
    
- **Row Expansion:** Typing in the row immediately below the table should automatically expand the table range to encompass the new row.
- Calculated column formulas should automatically propagate to the new row with relative references adjusted.
- Column number formatting, styles, and data validation rules should be inherited by the expanding row.
- **Column Expansion:** Typing in the column immediately to the right of the table should automatically add a new column to the table, creating a unique header if necessary.

### Actual Behavior

- The value is treated as a regular cell outside the table.
- The table's range remains unchanged (`A1:C3`).
- Formulas, data validation rules, and formats from the table are not propagated.
- The user must manually resize the table and manually copy down formulas.

title: Let an end user add a font without rebuilding
author: tonguyenducmanh
body:
## Ask

Let an end user add a font without rebuilding:

- **Paste a link** — Google Fonts `/css2?family=…`, any stylesheet with `@font-face`, or a direct
  `.ttf` / `.otf` / `.woff2` URL.
- **Upload a file** — drag-drop or picker.

On the web this is currently blocked at the source: there are no system fonts, nothing is bundled
beyond egui's Latin defaults, and changing it means a source edit.

## Current behaviour

GridCraft has the least font machinery of the four, which cuts both ways — more to build, but less
to integrate around.

- No `fonts` crate, no `craft-fonts` wiring.
- `crates/ui-egui/src/theme.rs` reads **system** font files from hardcoded `/usr/share/fonts/…`
  paths — on wasm there's nothing to read.
- The web shell avoids the problem rather than solving it:

  ```rust
  // apps/gridcraft-web/src/web.rs
  // Follow the browser's language, except a CJK one: the web build has no system
  // CJK fonts (none are bundled), so that interface would render as tofu.
  let browser = gridcraft_ui_egui::i18n::Language::system();
  if !matches!(browser, Language::Zh | Language::Ja | Language::Ko) {
      app.ui.language = browser;
  }
  ```

## Why this one matters most

`localization` is last on ROADMAP.md at 100–165 h, and much of that is presumably font coverage — a
spreadsheet UI can't localise into scripts it can't render. A user-installed font doesn't get
GridCraft to full localisation, but it does unblock the individual user immediately. Someone who
needs Japanese sheet names today simply can't use the app.

## Suggestion

If the full version is too big for the current milestone, a minimal one would be
`font.install_file` only (drop the URL path). `photocraft-web`'s `indexed_presets.rs` is a good
reference for the IndexedDB bridge — `MAX_STORE_BYTES`, the single whole-read deadline, and the RAII
`Listeners` that detach handlers on timeout.

body:
**gridcraft 0.5.0 (portable x64 zip and MSI, 2026-10-07 release) exits ~0.1 s after the window appears (exit code 1)** on Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26100, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 (driver 32.0.16.1088), DirectX 12 default backend.

Same root cause as storytold/craft-launcher#126 (opened the same day) and storytold/lightcraft#471 (fixed there by #484). title: [Bug] Resizing multiple Ctrl-selected rows or columns only affects the last selected item
author: aaronholoday
body:
**Description**

When multiple rows or columns are selected using Ctrl+click, resizing only affects the most recently selected row or column.

Resizing works for individual rows or columns and for an entire sheet selection, but not for a selection containing more than one and fewer than all rows or columns.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Open a worksheet in Gridcraft.
2. Click the header for column B.
3. Hold Ctrl and click the headers for columns D and F, leaving B, D, and F selected.
4. Resize column F using its header boundary.
5. Observe which columns change width.
6. Repeat the same process with nonadjacent rows to test row height.

**Expected behavior**

All selected columns should receive the new width, while unselected columns remain unchanged. In this example, columns B, D, and F should resize together; columns A, C, E, and all other unselected columns should retain their existing widths.

The same behavior should apply to row heights: resizing one selected row should apply the new height to all selected rows, without affecting unselected rows.

This would provide parity with Excel’s handling of multiple selected rows and columns.

**Actual behavior**

Only the most recently selected column or row is resized. Other selected columns or rows retain their previous dimensions.

**Impact**

Users must resize each row or column individually to give a selected subset consistent dimensions, making worksheet formatting unnecessarily repetitive.

**Tested on Version 0.5.0 on CachyOS**

title: Feature request: German-localized formula function names and separators
author: ScottGri
body:
## Summary

Thanks for adding the German interface language and Spanish formula localization (#45)! Could the same formula localization be added for German?

German Excel and LibreOffice users are used to German function names, `;` as the argument separator and `,` as the decimal separator. Right now GridCraft only accepts English syntax, so `=SUMME(A1;A3)` fails with "expected `,` or `)`, found Semicolon".

## Requested functionality

When the interface language is German, accept and display German function names, keeping English as the canonical/stored syntax (as with `FormulaLocale::Es`).

| German | English |
|---|---|
| `=SUMME(A1:A10)` | `=SUM(A1:A10)` |
| `=MITTELWERT(A1:A10)` | `=AVERAGE(A1:A10)` |
| `=WENN(A1>0;"Ja";"Nein")` | `=IF(A1>0,"Ja","Nein")` |
| `=ANZAHL(A1:A10)` | `=COUNT(A1:A10)` |
| `=SUMMEWENN(A1:A10;">0")` | `=SUMIF(A1:A10,">0")` |
| `=ZÄHLENWENN(A1:A10;">0")` | `=COUNTIF(A1:A10,">0")` |
| `=SVERWEIS(A2;D:E;2;FALSCH)` | `=VLOOKUP(A2,D:E,2,FALSE)` |
| `=XVERWEIS(...)` | `=XLOOKUP(...)` |
| `=RUNDEN(A1;2)` | `=ROUND(A1,2)` |
| `=HEUTE()` | `=TODAY()` |
| `WAHR` / `FALSCH` | `TRUE` / `FALSE` |

## Separators

- `;` as argument separator
- `,` as decimal separator (e.g. `=A1*1,5`)
- Array constants would probably also need German-Excel-compatible separators.

## Context

Tested on GridCraft 0.5.0 (Linux AppImage). The formula engine itself is great: everything from IFNA up to LAMBDA and REGEXTEST worked in English syntax.

title: VLOOKUP/XLOOKUP/LOOKUP return 0 instead of blank for an empty target cell (ISBLANK FALSE, concatenation inserts 0)
author: rex4539
body:
## Summary

When `VLOOKUP`, `XLOOKUP` or `LOOKUP` lands on an **empty** cell, GridCraft returns the number `0`. Excel returns a blank, so `ISBLANK()` of the result is `TRUE` and string concatenation treats it as `""`. In GridCraft `ISBLANK()` gives `FALSE` and concatenation inserts a literal `0`.

`INDEX`, `OFFSET` and `IF` returning an empty cell already behave like Excel, so the gap is specific to the lookup functions.

This breaks a common template pattern, `IF(ISBLANK(VLOOKUP(...)),"",VLOOKUP(...)&"...")`. In GridCraft every row whose lookup column is empty produces `"0..."` text instead of an empty string.

## Steps to reproduce

```python
# uv run --with openpyxl make.py
import openpyxl
wb = openpyxl.Workbook(); ws = wb.active
ws["A1"] = "k"; ws["A2"] = "j"; ws["B2"] = "v"   # B1 (the value for key "k") is empty
for i, f in enumerate([
    '=ISBLANK(VLOOKUP("k",A1:B2,2,0))',
    '="x"&VLOOKUP("k",A1:B2,2,0)&"y"',
    '=CONCATENATE("x",VLOOKUP("k",A1:B2,2,0),"y")',
    '=ISBLANK(XLOOKUP("k",A1:A2,B1:B2))',
    '="x"&XLOOKUP("k",A1:A2,B1:B2)&"y"',
    '=ISBLANK(LOOKUP("k",A1:A1,B1:B1))',
    '=ISBLANK(INDEX(B1:B2,1))',
    '=ISBLANK(IF(TRUE,B1))',
], 1):
    ws.cell(i, 4, f)
wb.save("blank_lookup.xlsx")
```

```
gridcraft-cli run --in blank_lookup.xlsx --cmd 'formulas.calculateNow={}' --print D1:D8
```

## Expected (Excel for Mac 16.78)

| Cell | Formula | Excel |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | `ISBLANK(VLOOKUP(...))` | `TRUE` |
| D2 | `"x"&VLOOKUP(...)&"y"` | `xy` |
| D3 | `CONCATENATE("x",VLOOKUP(...),"y")` | `xy` |
| D4 | `ISBLANK(XLOOKUP(...))` | `TRUE` |
| D5 | `"x"&XLOOKUP(...)&"y"` | `xy` |
| D6 | `ISBLANK(LOOKUP(...))` | `TRUE` |
| D7 | `ISBLANK(INDEX(...))` | `TRUE` |
| D8 | `ISBLANK(IF(TRUE,B1))` | `TRUE` |

A bare `=VLOOKUP("k",A1:B2,2,0)` still *displays* `0` in Excel. Only the value's blankness differs.

## Actual (GridCraft 0.5.0)

D1 `FALSE`, D2 `x0y`, D3 `x0y`, D4 `FALSE`, D5 `x0y`, D6 `FALSE`. D7 and D8 are correct (`TRUE`).

The same results come from th…

title: shrinkToFit alignment is ignored: text spills or is clipped, numbers show ###
author: rex4539
body:
## Summary

GridCraft ignores the cell alignment flag `shrinkToFit="1"`. When content is too wide for its cell, Excel shrinks the font until it fits. GridCraft instead draws it at full size:

- **Text** spills into the next empty cell, or is clipped.
- **Centred text in a merged range** is clipped on both sides, so the start and end of the sentence are lost.
- **Numbers** show as `###`.

Form-style templates (schedules, reports, invoices) rely on shrink-to-fit heavily. A workbook that looks correct in Excel can then show truncated labels and `###` in a large share of its cells.

## Steps to reproduce

```python
# uv run --with openpyxl make.py
import openpyxl
from openpyxl.styles import Alignment
wb = openpyxl.Workbook(); ws = wb.active
ws.column_dimensions["A"].width = 10
ws.column_dimensions["B"].width = 5
ws["A1"] = "Executive Producer"; ws["A1"].alignment = Alignment(shrinkToFit=True)
ws["A2"] = "Executive Producer"                       # control: no shrinkToFit
ws.merge_cells("A4:D4")
ws["A4"] = "THIS CENTRED SENTENCE IS MUCH TOO LONG FOR THE MERGED RANGE A4:D4"
ws["A4"].alignment = Alignment(horizontal="center", shrinkToFit=True)
ws["B6"] = 0.0; ws["B6"].number_format = "h:mm:ss"
ws["B6"].alignment = Alignment(horizontal="center", shrinkToFit=True)
wb.save("shrink.xlsx")
```

Open `shrink.xlsx` in the GridCraft desktop app.

## Expected (Excel for Mac 16.78)

- A1 is drawn in a smaller font, fully inside column A. A2, the control, spills into B as normal.
- A4 is drawn in a smaller font, and the whole sentence fits inside A4:D4.
- B6 shows `0:00:00` in a smaller font.

## Actual (GridCraft 0.5.0)

- A1 is drawn exactly like A2, spilling into column B.
- A4 is drawn at full size and clipped on both sides, so only the middle of the sentence shows.
- B6 shows `###`.

## Environment

GridCraft 0.5.0 desktop app, macOS 15.8.2 x86_64. Reference: Microsoft Excel for Mac 16.78.

title: Merged range border: right and bottom edges are not drawn (only the anchor cell's border is used)
author: rex4539
body:
## Summary

When a merged range has a border around it, GridCraft draws only the **top and left** edges. The right and bottom edges are missing.

Excel stores a merged range's outline on the cells along each edge: the right border on the last column's cells and the bottom border on the last row's cells. GridCraft appears to take the merged cell's border only from the top-left (anchor) cell, which carries just `left` and `top`. So a boxed merged range renders as an open "Γ" shape.

## Steps to reproduce

```python
# uv run --with openpyxl make.py
import openpyxl
from openpyxl.styles import Alignment, Border, Font, Side
wb = openpyxl.Workbook(); ws = wb.active
t = Side(style="thick")
ws.merge_cells("B2:E5")
ws["B2"] = "13:00"
ws["B2"].font = Font(size=36, bold=True)
ws["B2"].alignment = Alignment(horizontal="center", vertical="center")
for r in range(2, 6):
    for c in range(2, 6):
        ws.cell(r, c).border = Border(left=t if c == 2 else None, right=t if c == 5 else None,
                                      top=t if r == 2 else None, bottom=t if r == 5 else None)
wb.save("merged_border.xlsx")
```

This is the layout Excel itself writes when you merge B2:E5 and apply "Thick Outside Borders". Open the file in the GridCraft desktop app.

## Expected (Excel for Mac 16.78)

A closed thick box around B2:E5.

## Actual (GridCraft 0.5.0)

Only the top and left thick edges are drawn. The right edge (column E) and the bottom edge (row 5) are missing.

## Environment

GridCraft 0.5.0 desktop app, macOS 15.8.2 x86_64. Reference: Microsoft Excel for Mac 16.78.

title: Text box formatting ignored: run size/bold/font/outline, centre alignment, vertical anchor and noFill outline
author: rex4539
body:
## Summary

Text boxes (`xdr:sp` with `txBox="1"`) are drawn with default styling. GridCraft ignores what the drawing XML specifies:

- **Run properties** (`a:rPr`) are ignored: size (`sz="5400"`), bold, `a:latin` typeface, text fill and text outline (`a:ln` inside `a:rPr`). The text is drawn small, regular, black and in the default font.
- **Paragraph alignment** `a:pPr algn="ctr"` and **vertical anchor** `a:bodyPr anchor="ctr"` are ignored. The text sits in the top-left corner.
- **Shape outline** `a:spPr/a:ln/a:noFill` is ignored. A border is drawn around the box when there should be none.

Workbooks often use text boxes for large stamp-style labels such as "DRAFT" or a revision colour. In GridCraft these become small boxed captions.

## Steps to reproduce

The script below writes a minimal, valid workbook with one text box. Its drawing XML is the same as what Excel writes for a WordArt-style label.

```python
import zipfile
D = ('<xdr:wsDr xmlns:xdr="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/drawingml/2006/spreadsheetDrawing" '

author: marcbraun
body:
**Component:** `crates/xlsx` (`sheet_read.rs`) / `crates/calc` (`eval.rs`)
**Commit tested:** `1ea549b` (main, 2026-10-11)

A normal `<f>` formula whose cell has no `cm` attribute is a pre-dynamic-array

dependent of the top-left cell reads the wrong value.

This affects every workbook saved by Excel 2007–2016, by SheetJS, and by

title: CSV: saving a `;`-separated file rewrites it with `,` (separator detected on open is forgotten)
author: vedran-dobos
body:
### What happens

Open a semicolon-separated CSV (the usual "CSV" wherever `,` is the decimal separator — most of
continental Europe, Latin America, …) and save it: every `;` becomes `,`. The next program in the
chain can no longer read the file.

Reproduced on `main` (a513787) and 0.4.0 with a 74-row cut list exported by a furniture CAD/CAM
program (`;`-separated, CRLF, no BOM):

```
gridcraft-cli convert cutlist.csv out.csv
```

| | original | after save |
|---|---|---|
| row 1 | `1;720.0;579.0;K1_led_1;HDF_BIJELI;3.0;;;;;;` | `1,720,579,K1_led_1,HDF_BIJELI,3,,,,,,` |
| separator | `;` | `,` (all 74 rows) |

(The `720.0` → `720` and `1244121406E6` → `1.244121406E+15` changes in the same file are a separate
issue about data conversion and will be filed separately.)

### Cause

`read_csv` sniffs the delimiter (`sniff_delimiter`, `crates/xlsx/src/csv.rs`), but the result isn't
kept, and `save_bytes` (`crates/engine/src/io.rs`) calls `write_csv(sh, wb, b',')` with a
hard-coded comma. `file.save`, Save As `.csv`, `file.exportCsv`, `file.saveBytes` and
`gridcraft-cli convert` all go through that line.

### Expected

A workbook opened from CSV saves back with the separator it was opened with (Excel keeps a CSV in
its list-separator dialect too). Workbooks that didn't come from CSV keep today's `,`.

### Relation to open PRs

- #191 makes CSV save use the region's list separator. That helps when the region matches the
  file, but a comma file opened in a `;` region (or the reverse) would still be rewritten. The two
  fit together: the separator a file was opened with wins, otherwise the region's list separator.
- #422 (CSV writes displayed values) keeps the hard-coded `b','`, so it doesn't change this; the
  two touch the same line in `save_bytes`, a one-line rebase for whichever lands second.

I have a fix with regression tests ready and will open a PR referencing this issue.

title: Support Localized Excel Formula Names (Non-English Function Names)

body:
Currently, formula parsing appears to support only the English function names used by Excel. This creates friction for users working with localized versions of Excel, where function names and argument separators vary by language.

Add support for localized Excel function names and regional formula syntax.

Many users never interact with formulas in English because Microsoft localizes function names by language. Supporting localized formulas would significantly improve the experience for users in regions such as Latin America and Europe, where translated function names are the default behavior.

title: MCP server: add --automation-read-root / --automation-write-root, like VectorCraft
author: Dunai000
body:
## Runtime or environment

gridcraft-cli 0.5.0, macOS universal release build (commit 9f896c1).

## Summary

`gridcraft-cli mcp` gives the client agent the full file access of the user running it. `open_workbook`, `save_workbook`, `execute_command` (any engine command) and commands such as `file.saveAs`, `file.exportPdf`, `insert.picture` and CSV import take any path. A workbook carrying prompt-injected cell text can ask the agent to import a file from outside the working folder and read it back with `read_range`.

VectorCraft already solves this. Its `mcp` subcommand takes `--automation-read-root DIR` and `--automation-write-root DIR`, which confine every read and write the agent's commands make. In gridcraft-cli 0.5.0, `mcp` accepts only `--connect`, `--in` and `--sample` (`apps/gridcraft-cli/src/main.rs:493`), and passing the VectorCraft flags exits with "unknown option".

## Steps to reproduce

```sh
gridcraft-cli mcp --automation-read-root /tmp/work --automation-write-root /tmp/work
```

## Actual

The server exits: `gridcraft-cli: unknown option --automation-read-root`.

## Expected

The same two flags as VectorCraft, with the same rule that a root left out grants none of its access, so the server can be registered for an agent confined to one folder.
